A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PnP-CM research, with matching authors, core algorithm, and convergence theorem. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LSUN Bedroom and fastMRI reconstruction experiments, component ablations, and noise/NFE analyses in Tables 1–4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction experiments on LSUN Bedroom, CelebA-HQ, and fastMRI, including nonlinear tasks and additional ablation and sensitivity results.

M1.justification: v2 implements nonlinear data-fidelity optimization, including a differentiable JPEG surrogate, whereas v1 left nonlinear implementation to future work. Supplement B.1 also adds phase-retrieval output disambiguation and specifies median-filter initialization for inpainting, contrasting with v1's explicit zero-initialization/no-heuristics description. The ADMM-CM core remains; the explicit CM noise-scale parameter mainly formalizes separately tuned noise levels already mentioned in v1.

E1.justification: v2 adds CelebA-HQ training and evaluation and evaluates JPEG restoration, nonlinear deblurring, and coded-mask phase retrieval on both natural-image datasets. LSUN Bedroom's original linear restoration tasks and fastMRI PD/PD-FS reconstruction remain.

E2.justification: Linear natural-image comparisons add DiffPIR, DPnP, and PnP-DM. The new nonlinear comparisons evaluate DPS, ΠGDM, and DPnP. MRI comparisons now include quantitative and visual CM4IR results alongside DPS and DDS; v1 only described CM4IR's failure without corresponding comparative entries.

E3.justification: The reported MRI CM distillation budget changes from 7M iterations in v1 Appendix D.1 to 700k in v2 Supplement C; this establishes a revised stated setting, without establishing retraining. New protocols include CelebA-HQ training/evaluation splits, JPEG quality factor 5, eight-NFE phase retrieval, MRI momentum controls at 4/10/20 NFEs, and randomized hyperparameter perturbations up to 25%.

E4.justification: v2 adds an MRI study testing whether momentum benefits diminish with increasing NFEs and a CelebA-HQ deblurring hyperparameter-sensitivity study (Supplement D.1–D.2). The four-way component ablation and noise/NFE sweep move from LSUN Bedroom experiments to CelebA-HQ experiments, replacing their evidence rather than merely relocating it.

E5.justification: Both versions use averaged reconstruction metrics and retain plus/minus reporting for MRI. Neither introduces seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new randomized sensitivity study changes experimental design without adding uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive CelebA-HQ, nonlinear-task, baseline, and sensitivity results while revising retained entries. For example, four-NFE LSUN deblurring changes from 28.10/0.237 to 27.49/0.285 PSNR/LPIPS, and MRI PD R=4 PnP-CM mean PSNR changes from 32.69 to 35.57. These are revised reported results, not established controlled performance gains. Original two-NFE comparator entries and LSUN ablation/sweep results are removed or replaced.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 removes v1's specialized empirical ODE, dx/dt = -t sϕ, and instead describes sampling through the general drift/diffusion probability-flow equation. This is a limited mathematical-formulation revision. Theorem 1, its Lipschitz and summable-noise assumptions, and Appendix A's convergence argument remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion broaden the work from demonstrated linear restoration/MRI reconstruction to a unified framework with demonstrated linear and nonlinear applications. Nonlinear implementation was explicitly future work in v1. The proximal-prior interpretation, few-NFE efficiency, and first MRI-trained CM claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 removes the LSUN-only limitation and nonlinear-future-work discussion as coverage expands. It adds interpretations of comparable visual quality to diffusion-PnP methods, robustness to hyperparameter perturbations, and phase-retrieval ambiguity. Its new MRI analysis qualifies momentum as especially useful at low NFEs and not the primary performance driver, replacing v1's emphasis on momentum dominance in its LSUN ablation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, explicit noise/penalty/momentum schedules, coefficient values for CelebA-HQ and MRI in Table 3, nonlinear implementation instructions, additional baseline tuning details, and training losses and budgets. v1 largely described empirical tuning and referenced external implementations. Conversely, v1's explicit [0,1] input-normalization statement is no longer stated.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 replaces the Schrödinger-bridge discussion of I2SB/CDDB with substantive positioning against diffusion-based PnP approaches, including newly cited work by Graikos, Park, Wu, and Xu/Chi. v2 also expands nonlinear-imaging references and more explicitly positions noise and momentum as established acceleration techniques, including momentum-ADMM prior work.

P1.justification: The abstract, contributions, related-work discussion, acceleration narrative, and results discussion are substantially rewritten. v2 introduces separate Final Algorithm and Ablation Studies subsections, removes the standalone Discussion section, and reorganizes the appendices into experimental details, training details, and further results. These changes extend beyond renaming and renumbering.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, redraws the introductory overview, and merges the original natural-image and MRI tables into an expanded multipart Table 1. It adds nonlinear comparisons, a sensitivity plot, and CelebA-HQ image grids. Retained LSUN and MRI grids are expanded with comparator columns and rearranged; new hyperparameter and momentum tables further change the presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation and reproducibility: it addresses v1's acknowledged narrow natural-image coverage and untested nonlinear extension, adds relevant diffusion-PnP comparisons, and documents tuning with sensitivity evidence and explicit coefficients. These gains outweigh the loss of some original LSUN analyses. Important gaps remain: Table 3 omits LSUN coefficients, and broad superiority wording is not supported uniformly across Table 1's metrics.
